risk.title: Risk appetite
risk.subtitle: What each factor of an asset's risk score is worth, and where this institution draws the line it calls high risk.
risk.notChosen: Your assets are scored under the platform's standard values. They are a reasonable starting point and they are not your decision — an auditor asking why a server scores 8.4 is asking about your appetite, not ours.
risk.chosen: Based on the {preset} profile. Every version is kept with its dates, so what the formula was on a given day stays answerable.
risk.presetsHelp: Pick the one whose reporting fits the institution, then move the two or three factors it argues with. The fields are fixed and the weights are not: that is what keeps a score explainable.
risk.notes: Why this is what you chose
risk.notesHelp: An auditor reads this before they read the weights.
risk.notesPlaceholder: e.g. the SWIFT perimeter carries our attestation, so it weighs above card scope this year
risk.changedCount: {count, plural, =0 {No factor moved from the standard} one {# factor moved from the standard} other {# factors moved from the standard}}
risk.saved: Recorded. Asset scores are produced under this version from now on; the previous one keeps its dates.
risk.historyHelp: Each version, with the window it was in force. This is the answer to what the formula was on a given day.
risk.noHistory: This tenant has recorded no version yet.
risk.readOnly: You can read this appetite but not change it. Setting a risk appetite needs the risk:write permission, which the risk function holds rather than the tenant administrator.

criticality_step.label: Per criticality level

criticality_cap.label: Criticality ceiling

vuln_cap.label: Vulnerability ceiling
vuln_cap.help: The most open findings can contribute, however many there are.

exposure_cap.label: Exposure ceiling
exposure_cap.help: The most regulated exposure can contribute in total.

never_seen.label: Never scanned

critical_production.label: Critical in production

banking_type.label: Banking asset type
banking_type.help: Added for an asset type specific to banking.

high_risk_threshold.label: High risk from
high_risk_threshold.help: The score at and above which this institution calls an asset high risk. It is what the counts and the reports are drawn on.

remediation.baseHelp: Days from when the finding was first seen — not from the last scan, so a re-scan never buys more time.
remediation.ceilingsHelp: A condition can bring a deadline forward, never push one out. Several at once take the tightest. Leave one off and that condition is treated no differently.
remediation.changedCount: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing moved from the standard} one {# value moved from the standard} other {# values moved from the standard}}
remediation.chosen: Based on the {preset} policy. Every version keeps its dates, so whether a finding breached its deadline stays a question about the policy in force when it was raised.
remediation.floorHelp: No combination goes below this. A deadline of zero days is not a commitment, it is a breach recorded the moment the finding is.
remediation.historyHelp: Each version with the window it was in force. Whether a finding breached its deadline is a claim about the policy in force when it was raised.
remediation.noHistory: This tenant has recorded no version yet.
remediation.notChosen: Your findings are given the platform's standard deadlines. They are a reasonable starting point and they are not your commitment — a regulator asking why a critical stayed open for a week is asking about yours, not ours.
remediation.notes: Why this is what you chose
remediation.notesHelp: An auditor reads this before they read the numbers.
remediation.notesPlaceholder: e.g. our card perimeter carries a contractual 14-day commitment this year
remediation.presetsHelp: The figures are our reading of what these regimes ask for, meant to be argued with by someone who knows the institution's own commitments. A starting point, not a citation.
remediation.readOnly: You can read these deadlines but not change them. Setting them needs the vulnerabilities:write permission.
remediation.saved: Recorded. The previous version keeps its dates.
remediation.subtitle: How long this institution gives itself to fix something. Not a fact about a vulnerability: a commitment, to a regulator, to a card scheme, or to its own board.
remediation.title: Remediation deadlines

attack.base_cost: Any step, before anything is known
attack.breadthHelp: Added as boost × ln(1 + paths), so the tenth route counts less than the second. Zero means the number of ways in does not move the scenario's risk at all.
attack.changedCount: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing moved from the standard} one {# value moved from the standard} other {# values moved from the standard}}
attack.chosen: Based on the {preset} stance. Every scenario records which version scored it, so a risk figure in a report stays reproducible after the stance moves.
attack.complexity_high: Added for a technique of high complexity
attack.complexity_medium: Added for a technique of medium complexity
attack.cost: What a step costs an attacker
attack.costHelp: Cost is friction, not danger: a step you consider harder makes the path that uses it rank lower. An edge the platform knows nothing about keeps the cost it was imported with.
attack.distanceHelp: A decay of 1.00 is the assume-breach position stated exactly: once inside, distance is not a control.
attack.historyHelp: Each version with the window it was in force. Why a path ranked second in March is a question about the weightings of March.
attack.hop_decay: Each extra hop multiplies the threat by
attack.impact: What reaching a target is worth
attack.impactHelp: The ceiling is normally below 10 so the critical-system bonus has somewhere to go. What an unrecorded target is worth is a stance of its own: high treats the unknown as dangerous, which is safer and noisier.
attack.impact_ceiling: Most a target's criticality can be worth
attack.many_paths_boost: Weight given to the number of ways in
attack.noHistory: This tenant has recorded no version yet.
attack.notChosen: Your paths are ranked on the platform's stance. A team that has watched a red team cross the estate in an afternoon does not weigh difficulty the way one reasoning from CVSS does.
attack.notes: Why this is what you chose
attack.notesHelp: An auditor reads this before they read the numbers.
attack.notesPlaceholder: e.g. the September red team crossed the estate in an afternoon; distance does not protect us
attack.presetsHelp: Pick the one that matches how this institution reasons about an attacker, then move what it argues with. Each stance re-ranks every scenario the next time it runs.
attack.privilege_high: Added when the step needs administrative rights
attack.privilege_low: Added when the step needs some privilege
